summary: Taiki Mibu earned a PhD from Ryukoku University by 2016 in Buddhist studies. Mibu was attested as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University in 2015.

Taikyo Tanigawa works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at Koyasan University and earned a PhD from Toyo University by 1994. Tanigawa has held positions including associate professor and professor at Koyasan University, attested between 1980 and 2026.
Taion Satomi studied at Rissho University until 1933 in the field of Buddhist studies. Satomi later served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College, attested in 1972.

Taira Shidehara was an archaeologist and historian who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1895 to 1898. Shidehara held posts at the University of Tokyo around 1900 to 1906 and Tokyo University of Education around 1902 to 1906.

Tairyō Makita worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology, studying under Shinryo Iwai and at Otani, Kyoto, and Bukkyo universities. Makita held posts at Kyoto University, Saitama Institute of Technology as president, and Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University.
Taisen Deshimaru was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied under Kodo Sawaki from circa 1936 to 1965. Deshimaru founded the Association Zen Internationale and La Gendronnière.

Taishu Tagami is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. Tagami served as a professor at Komazawa University from circa 1970 to 2006 and lectured at Toho Gakuin in 1990.
Taishun Mibu specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying at Taisho University from circa 1934 to 1937. Mibu later served as library director at Taisho University from circa 1952 to 1979.

Taitetsu Unno was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned degrees from UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo. Unno served as Jill Ker Conway Professor Emeritus of Religion at Smith College from 1971 to 1998.
Taitsu Kono studied at Hanazono University from circa 1950 to 1954 and trained under Mumon Yamada from circa 1954 to 1988. In the field of Buddhist studies, Kono held a post at Hanazono University.

Taixu was a Buddhist studies and philosophy figure who studied under Jing'an, Jichan, and Yang Wenhui at Jinling Scriptural Press. He led the Minnan Buddhist Institute and founded multiple Buddhist institutes, the Chinese Buddhist Association, and the World Fellowship of Buddhists.
Tak Pui Sze works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Sze earned a PhD from the University of British Columbia, where doctoral studies were supervised by Jinhua Chen (attested 2012).

Taka Yanagisawa was an art historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Japan Women's University from circa 1945 to 1948. Yanagisawa served as Director of the Department of Fine Arts at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1953–1988).

Takaaki Yoshimoto studied at Yamagata University (~1943–1944) and Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1944–1947). Active in philosophy, Yoshimoto held a post at Tokyo Institute of Technology from circa 1947 to 1950.

Takahiko Kameyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. Kameyama's attested posts in 2015 include professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.
Takahiko Sato works in Buddhist studies. Sato held a post as professor at Koyasan University, attested in 2015 and 2026.

Takahiro Kato is an Indology and philosophy scholar with a Dr.Phil from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg. Kato holds posts at the University of Tokyo as professor and at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, attested in 2026.

Takaji Fukita specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at Taisho University under Zenno Ishigami, Bukkyo University under Shozen Kumoi and Yuichi Kajiyama, and under Heinz Bechert. Fukita served as a lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 1997–2010).
Takako Abe works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Abe served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2013–2017) and remains on the faculty there as attested in 2026.

Takamaro Shigaraki studied at Ryukoku University, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and the Institute of Buddhist Studies. In Buddhist studies, Shigaraki served as professor and president of Ryukoku University (1989–1995) and led the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism.
